{{Top}}
[[File:PlasteelCylinders-KOTOR.png|thumb|left|Plasteel cylinders in the [[Tarisian military base|Sith Base on Taris]]]]
'''Plasteel''', sometimes called '''plastisteel''', was a material that combined acrylic [[Polymer/Legends|polymer]]s and metal alloys. Plasteel retained the elastic strength of plastics while benefiting from the strength and heat resistance of metal. Plasteel was most commonly used in armor, [[Starship/Legends|spaceship]] components, containers, and construction. It was capable of yellowing with age.<ref name="Shadow Hunter">''[[Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter]]''</ref>

Military-grade plasteel made capable armor, able to withstand heavy assault weapons and explosives, and was used extensively in the [[MI-series security droid]].<ref name="EndlessVigil">''[[Endless Vigil]]''</ref> [[Vector Technologies]] was a company that specialized in military-grade plasteel, and produced plasteel that was strong enough to withstand a [[Thermal detonator/Legends|thermal detonator]], but was as light as [[polythin]].<ref name="WretchedHive">''[[Wretched Hives of Scum & Villainy]]''</ref> [[PD-series protocol droid]]s had their [[powerbus cable]]s sealed behind plasteel plating. The [[Scarab Mark VI assassin droid]]'s body casing was made of armored plasteel. [[EVS Construction Droid]]s were capable of producing plasteel girders for building structures.<ref name="EGTD">''[[The Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The word ''plasteel'' is a portmanteau of ''plastic'' and ''steel''. The term appears in Frank Herbert's [[Wikipedia:Dune universe|''Dune'']] series and may have been coined by [[Wikipedia:Harlan Ellison|Harlan Ellison]], who used it as early as 1956.
